title: Carbon dioxide at Mauna Loa rose every year from 1959 to 2019
subtitle: annual means of the seasonally adjusted monthly record · up 95.5 ppm in all; the smallest yearly rise was 0.35 ppm
data: Mauna Loa monthly CO2, NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory and Scripps Institution of Oceanography, 1958-2020, via vega-datasets 2.8.0

title: Every colour is defined once, in vellum.json, and every style file derives from it
subtitle: how the files of Vellum are made · an arrow points from a file to what is made from it
data: the repository's own generators/ and style/ folders
alt: A left-to-right diagram: build_palettes.py searches OKLCH for the tone lightness and writes palettes.json; make_vellum_json.py turns it into vellum.json, the source of truth; make_assets.py generates vellum.mplstyle, vellum.R, vellum-colors.sty, vellum.css and vellum-office.tsv, and the hand-written vellum.py reads vellum.json at run time; the files feed matplotlib, ggplot2, pgfplots, TikZ and beamer, the web, and Office and Canva.

title: Within each species longer beaks are deeper; pooled, the trend reverses
subtitle: 342 penguins, Palmer Archipelago, 2007–2009 · least-squares fits with 95 % bands, labelled with their slope in mm per mm
data: Palmer penguins, Gorman, Williams and Fraser (2014), PLoS ONE 9(3): e90081; Palmer Station LTER; via vega-datasets 2.8.0
alt: A scatter plot of beak depth against beak length for 342 penguins: within Adélie, Chinstrap and Gentoo the fitted slopes are +0.18, +0.22 and +0.20 mm per mm, while one line through all three species slopes at −0.09.
note: Simpson's paradox: the pooled trend reverses the trend inside every species.

title: Past a carrying capacity of 2.33, a richer habitat turns a stable equilibrium into boom and bust
subtitle: Rosenzweig–MacArthur predator–prey model · two phase planes and the bifurcation in K
data: Rosenzweig–MacArthur model (Rosenzweig 1971), integrated with SciPy; densities scaled
alt: Three panels. a: the phase plane at K = 2, with a direction field, the prey and predator nullclines and an orbit spiralling into the stable equilibrium at N = 0.67, P = 1.11. b: at K = 3 the equilibrium is unstable and orbits join a limit cycle on which the predator swings from 0.54 to 1.96. c: the predator against K; the equilibrium is stable up to a Hopf bifurcation at K = 2.33, after which the cycle widens to 0.20–2.98 at K = 4.5.
note: a model, not data: the paradox of enrichment (Rosenzweig 1971).

title: Even perfect nest survival cannot halt the loggerhead decline; better survival at sea can
subtitle: stage-structured model of a Georgia population · λ = 0.945, a decline of 5.5 % a year
data: stage matrix of Crouse, Crowder and Caswell (1987), Ecology 68, 1412–1423; data/ecology/loggerhead_crouse1987.csv
alt: a: the seven-stage life cycle of loggerhead turtles, from eggs and hatchlings to mature breeders, with arrows for staying, growing and reproducing, each as wide as its elasticity of λ; staying as a mature breeder has the largest, 0.230. b: the elasticities summed by stage. c: λ when the annual survival of one stage is raised: even 100 % survival of eggs and hatchlings gives λ = 0.965, while λ reaches 1 with 17 % better survival of mature breeders, 20 % of small juveniles, 24 % of subadults or 27 % of large juveniles.

title: Faster growth drives a population from a steady state through period doubling into chaos
subtitle: Ricker map · the steady state gives way at r = 2, the Lyapunov exponent turns positive at r = 2.69
form: bifurcation diagram, Lyapunov exponent and time series
data: Ricker map (Ricker 1954; May 1976), iterated in prepare_data.py
alt: a: the long-run population sizes of the Ricker map for growth rates r from 1.6 to 3.6, one steady state up to r = 2, then a two-cycle, a four-cycle and chaos from r = 2.69. b: the Lyapunov exponent on the same axis, negative while periodic and positive in chaos. c: three populations over 40 generations at r = 1.8, 2.4 and 3.0: a steady state, a two-cycle and chaos.
